# Delivery routing ruling (e2e synthetic)

Tanya (team owner) ruled on where reaction delivery belongs:

> we route every reaction through one bundle per run per person, not one
> message per skill — a person should get one thing to read, not four

Tina pushed back on the batching window and Tanya held: the bundle closes when
the run closes, and a skill that misses the close waits for the next run rather
than sending on its own. The alternative considered and rejected was per-skill
delivery with client-side collapsing, which moves the ordering problem onto the
reader.

payload.rationale: The document is a delivery-routing ruling that touches the product's delivery architecture, batching strategy, and async-vs-real-time positioning. I expanded Position_WebhookArchitecture and Obs_ZephyrRateLimitResolved because the ruling's server-side batching and run-close window directly extend the webhook event-driven architecture and the prior batched-delivery rate-limit fix. Position_ZephyrIntegrationUnlock provides the integration context for where reactions are delivered. The core narratives — DecisionCaptureAtConsensus, DecisionsEvaporate, AntiSlackPositioning — and their positions (CoreFeatureDecisionCapture, AntiPatternRealtimeChat, ProductCategoryAsyncPlatform) frame the 'one thing to read, not four' ruling as an instance of the anti-Slack, structured-async thesis. Position_ContextPreservationNextSprint and Position_Sprint4ThesisProven connect the ruling to the next-sprint context-preservation focus and the validated thesis. I deliberately did NOT expand the pricing positions (PricingTwelveDollars, PricingTier25Plus) or TargetMarketRemoteTeams — delivery routing has no bearing on pricing or segmentation. The Actor_Tanya_Staging hub was also skipped as it is a repetitive test artifact with no substantive content.
